runs.label: smoke
runs.note: Smoke run that proves the pipeline end to end: one case, one run per arm. It is too small to compare the arms. The eval shell could not start on the recording machine (the kernel restricts nested user namespaces), so no run could execute its tests and `tests-run` fails in both arms; the outcome checks ran the tests afterwards.

runs.label: pilot
runs.note: Grader calibration pilot of the six `hard` cases after the outcome checks were added: one run per arm, so no row is evidence of a difference between the arms. The eval shell could not start on the recording machine either, so `tests-run` here only shows that a test command was issued; `inconclusive` means the run's tests need pytest, which was not installed where the outcome checks ran.

runs.label: proof-1.6.0
runs.note: Proof run on arsenal 1.6.0 (branch feat/arsenal-smart): all 11 task cases, 5 runs per arm, with and without the plugin, model sonnet, judge haiku, on the maintainer's machine with the OS sandbox working (Bash ran in both arms). Outcome checks ran afterwards with pytest installed. Costs include judge calls.

runs.label: smart-sonnet
runs.note: Calibration of the four smart-* cases (built to catch plausible wrong fixes; unit tests prove each wrong fix fails acceptance): 3 runs per arm, model sonnet; no OS sandbox, so Bash was not granted and tests ran only in the outcome checks. Both arms passed acceptance 3/3 on every case, so these cases do not separate the arms on this model.

runs.label: smart-haiku
runs.note: Same four smart-* cases on model haiku, 3 runs per arm, same conditions. Both arms passed acceptance 3/3 on every case: the weaker model also solves them without the plugin.

runs.label: smart-sonnet-short-listing
runs.note: The four smart-* cases after the skill descriptions were cut from about 24,100 to 7,800 characters (trigger phrases moved to a routing comment the router reads), 3 runs per arm, model sonnet, no OS sandbox. Acceptance 3/3 in both arms, as before; the with-plugin arm costs about 22 percent less than in smart-sonnet, and its first call carries about 20,900 input tokens against 25,600 before.
